findings.decompiled: if 0 >= stor17.length: revert with 0x5428d449, _to / mem[0] = 17 / _3 = sha3(17) / s = 0 / while -_to + address(stor[_3 + s]): if SafeMath.inc(s) >= stor17.length: revert with 0x5428d449, _to; mem[0] = 17; _3 = sha3(17); s = SafeMath.inc(s)
findings.source: VRFCoordinatorV2_5.sol:722 for (uint256 i = 0; i < migrationTargetsLength; ++i) if (s_migrationTargets[i] == target) return true; (then revert CoordinatorNotRegistered)
findings.issue: The rotated search loop is correct but its condition is a subtraction used as a truth value, the element is stor[_3 + s] instead of stor17[s] (the array hash was bound to a temporary), and SafeMath.inc(s) and sha3(17) are recomputed in the body.
findings.rule: Print 'while a - b' (or '-b + a') as 'while a != b'; print stor[sha3(n) + i] as the array element storn[i] also when sha3(n) is held in a temporary; hoist loop-invariant sha3 of constants.

findings.decompiled: while s >= 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffefffffc2f: ... / while addmod(mulmod(_179, mulmod(_179, _179, -4294968273), -4294968273), 7, -4294968273) != mulmod(...)
findings.issue: The secp256k1 field modulus prints as a hex word in comparisons and as the negative decimal -4294968273 in addmod/mulmod, so the same constant is not recognisable as the same; the loops themselves are clear.
findings.rule: Print a constant in one form throughout a function; prefer the unsigned hex form for values above 2**255 used as unsigned operands (mulmod/addmod moduli are unsigned).

notes: Source loops (11), all whiles: _deleteSubscription, VRF._fieldHash (1168, 1234), VRF._hashToCurve (1225), _isTargetRegistered (migrate, rotated with the bound check inside), pendingRequestExists (and its inlined copies), deregisterMigratableCoordinator, deregisterProvingKey, fulfillRandomWords' numWords loop, getActiveSubscriptionIds, migrate's consumers loop, removeConsumer's search (swap-and-pop). Implicit: uint256[2] proof copies with constant trip count 2 (P7, 'while idx < 2'), storage arrays copied to memory as rotated whiles (P3), return encodings. Packed subscription/consumer structs are written through memory slices ('uint64(stor4[caller][..].field_8) = mem[184 len 8]', P18). VRF elliptic-curve arithmetic and the billing (native/LINK) paths follow the source.
summary: Faithful, all eleven loops present and readable; small issues are subtraction-as-condition, array elements via temporaries, and one modulus printed two ways.
